##### SUMMARY
`_load_config_defs` has a small performance hit which grows on larger inventories. This changes it so that it is only called when needed while also causing it to call for both the short_name or fqcn module names so that other calls by fqcn do not break. E.g. #77669

Fixes #78795

issue_context.body:
### Summary

Dynamic inventories have grown particularly slow when they load up a large number of machines. Our inventory of 10k+ nodes is taking a little over 60 seconds from command start to the first ansible task running - assuming a fully cached local inventory which skips the fetch calls.

The issue appears to have started somewhere around Ansible 4.
Edit: Updated to highlight the core 2.11.11 -> 2.11.12 2x speed increase. I'm still searching for a way to find where the 3.4 -> 4.0 one may be.

For the core 2.11.11 -> 2.11.12 regression, a3cc6a581ef191faf1c9ec102d1c116c4c2a8778 appears to be the cause. (https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/77696 for 2.11.11)

@bcoca I could be misreading things, but was moving `_load_config_defs` calls L814/L946 outside of if in cache blocks intentional? Pushing the load back so it only happens if not previously cached brings the speed back.

yes as plugins can be loaded via multiple paths and this fixed an issue with config not being defined correctly when an alias was used. I'm not sure why that should slow down things so much since we do condition actual loading to the config not existing/being cached.

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/a3cc6a581ef191faf1c9ec102d1c116c4c2a8778/lib/ansible/plugins/loader.py#L386-L401
At least in our case, the caching in that function isn't working. We see thousands of the `Loaded config def from plugin (vars/host_group_vars)` line if run in debug mode. Counted >20k loaded called for one single run. 
`C.config.get_configuration_definition(type_name, name)` returns `None` so it always goes down into the block and starts adding frags and configuring the plugin.

The original change said `plugin loader will now load config data for plugin by name instead of by file to avoid issues with the same file being loaded under different names (fqcn + short name)` which I was understanding as trying to stop a call to both `ansible.base.some_function` and `some_function` in a play from loading the config twice, however from #77669 it looks like the fqcn can't access the config because of the loader behaviour.

So one possible solution would be to track what names have been loaded and reload the config if a call handles on a name not previously loaded. This brings back most of the speed from this change.

Something like this instead of https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/a3cc6a581ef191faf1c9ec102d1c116c4c2a8778/lib/ansible/plugins/loader.py#L820-L824
```
        if path not in self._module_cache or name not in self._loaded_module_names:
            self._module_cache[path] = self._load_module_source(name, path)
            self._load_config_defs(name, self._module_cache[path], path)
            self._loaded_module_names.append(name)
            found_in_cache = False
```
It'd still re-load the config defs for `ansible.base.some_function` and `some_function` twice, but it is already doing that now. Does that seem acceptable?

Added a PR #78856 for easier review. In current testing this restores all of the performance lost since 3.4 for us on the existing calls. We still lose some performance on everyday `ansible-playbook` calls but I've not located that part yet.

we already have this data and we should not keep additional cache, if the current config query is not working correctly we just need to fix that.

also this only changes one of many paths to load a plugin, they all need to be consistent.

```
{'/usr/lib/python3.8/site-packages/ansible/plugins/cache/memory.py': <module 'ansible.plugins.cache.memory' from '/usr/lib/python3.8/site-packages/ansible/plugins/cache/memory.py'>}

So while we could check for that call in that cache, it won't help us know if the short_name was previously called and loaded. If there is a way I can access the originally called name in that cache or if it is in another cache please let me know and I can adjust things.

As for consistency, this is just trying to bring back the performance lost from the original change a3cc6a581ef191faf1c9ec102d1c116c4c2a8778 which only changed these two areas.
